idempotency.text: Idempotency in payment APIs means one logical payment keeps one outcome. For example, retry POST /payments after a timeout; the service returns the stored result without a second charge.

A payment endpoint is idempotent when repeated requests represent one operation. If the client sends the request again, it reuses the identifier and receives the previous result instead of duplicate processing.
Idempotency in payments prevents duplicate work. Retry requests should be handled carefully.
Idempotency in payment APIs means requests can be repeated safely. For example, retry POST /payments after a timeout.
For example, retry POST /payments with the same identifier and return the original result without charging twice.

architecture_authority.text: PostgreSQL is the source of truth. Redis and Valkey are non-authoritative caches.
PostgreSQL is the system of record; Redis and Valkey are not authoritative.
PostgreSQL is authoritative. Redis is cache only and Valkey is queue only.
PostgreSQL owns the durable state. Redis is not canonical, and Valkey does not own durable state.
PostgreSQL is the source of truth. Neither Redis nor Valkey is the system of record.
Redis is the authoritative store and PostgreSQL keeps a replica.
